bahai: a teacher of or believer in Bahaism
bahaism: a religion founded in Iran in 1863; emphasizes the spiritual unity of all humankind; incorporates Christian and Islamic tenets; many adherents live in the United States
Bahaism has no public rituals or sacraments and praying is done in private
bahamas: island country in the Atlantic to the east of Florida and Cuba; a popular winter resort
bahamian: a native or inhabitant of the Bahamas
of or relating to or characteristic of the Bahama Islands or their inhabitants
bahasa: the dialect of Malay used as the national language of the Republic of Indonesia or of Malaysia
bahrain: an island in the Persian Gulf
an island country in the Persian Gulf off the coast of Saudi Arabia; oil revenues funded progressive programs until reserves were exhausted in 1970s
bahraini: a native or inhabitant of Bahrain
of or relating to or characteristic of Bahrain or its people or language
bahrein: an island in the Persian Gulf
an island country in the Persian Gulf off the coast of Saudi Arabia; oil revenues funded progressive programs until reserves were exhausted in 1970s
bahreini: a native or inhabitant of Bahrain
baht: the basic unit of money in Thailand
